summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood and Veridian focused on building a connector and short sandbox pilot. Veridian wants a lightweight integration that can route customer inference to their GPU fabric and optionally fall back to Redwood hosted capacity. Key constraints: multi-tenant tenancy on Veridian side, network/VPC peering model, SOC2 evidence, and pilot target of supporting an initial workload of 200 QPS peak with mixed sequence lengths. Agreed next steps: Redwood to provision sandbox instructions and perf guide; Veridian to share instance details and compliance contacts; schedule deep-dive benchmark week of Oct 4.

transcript:
Meeting Header: 2026-09-24 15:00 UTC | Duration 48m | Redwood: Samir, Maya, Alex | Veridian: Liam, Priya, Jorge

Auto-generated Summary: quick partner intro; scope connector + sandbox pilot; follow ups listed below.

[00:00] Samir Patel: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, i'm Samir from Redwood - i run channel partnerships, with me is Maya our solutions engineer and Alex on the systems team. how's everyone doing?
[00:06] Liam O'Connor: yeah thanks Samir, good, excited to chat. i'm Liam, head of platform at Veridian. we've been looking to add a tight connector to help our customers spin up inference closer to their data.
[00:12] Priya Menon: hi all, Priya here - solutions architect - we'll be your primary technical contact.
[00:16] Jorge Alvarez: Jorge, partnerships, quick intro and then i'll be mostly listening for commercial fit.
[00:21] Maya Chen: awesome, thanks. goal for today is to understand Veridian's GPU fabric, network model, security requirements, and sketch out a sandbox pilot. we'll also highlight where Redwood Dedicated and Redwood Private differ for this use case.
[00:33] Samir Patel: quick note — we put together a short deck and onboarding doc, link in the notes: https://redwood.com/link/veridian-connector-deck (shared).
[00:40] Liam O'Connor: saw that, thanks. high level from our side — we run a multi-tenant GPU pool across sites, we expose tenant networks via V P C peering and a lightweight proxy. curious if Redwood can run a connector that routes calls to our pool and optionally failover to Redwood hosted.
[00:56] Alex Graves: yes, technically that's straightforward. Redwood's runtime supports policy-based routing — you can route by latency or cost. one nuance is auth and key rotation when the control plane sits in your V P C; we typically integrate with customer KMS or we can bring a federated key model.
[01:15] Priya Menon: ok on KMS — we use Vault and HSM for customer keys, so we'd want to keep tokenization inside our perimeter if possible. also SOC2 is table stakes for our customers, so we'll need audit logs and evidence.
[01:27] Maya Chen: we can support customer-managed KMS and we stream audit logs to your SIEM. small caveat: if you want Redwood to run the control plane in your V P C we call that Redwood Private and it requires slightly different onboarding and licensing.
[01:40] Liam O'Connor: what's the minimal pilot setup you'd recommend? we want to validate routing and basic perf first.
[01:45] Maya Chen: for an initial sandbox we usually do: connector container + auth layer deployed in your test V P C, a small pool of GPUs (we can test with 2-4 GPUs), and a synthetic benchmark using your sequence distributions. that'll validate latency, throughput, and error handling.
[01:58] Jorge Alvarez: who owns the connector code? we want flexibility to extend it for our managed customers.
[02:03] Samir Patel: good question — the connector is open API-based. for the sandbox Redwood will provide the containerized connector and docs; for long term we can license the connector or provide an OEM SDK. you can fork/adapt under the partner terms. we'll send the devops quickstart.
[02:20] Priya Menon: perfect. two more constraints — we need to avoid cross-tenant KV cash leaks, and we want to ensure the batching policy respects tenant boundaries.
[02:31] Maya Chen: yep that's critical. our runtime supports tenant-aware batching and KV cache isolation per customer. note: sometimes transcriptions in previous docs call KV 'K-V cash' — but technically we keep the cache logically partitioned.
[02:45] Liam O'Connor: i saw references to your optimize tool — can that recommend quantization profiles? we've got a mix of LLMs (open LLaMA forks + a couple of larger encoder-decoder models).
[02:56] Alex Graves: Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization and batching per-model; in a pilot we typically run small experiments on 8-bit quant vs fp16 to see quality regression. we can include a quick eval harness as part of the sandbox.
[03:10] Priya Menon: timeline — we'd like to run a pilot in early october, ideally first week. is that feasible?
[03:15] Maya Chen: yes — if we get instance types and your expected qps distribution this week we can prep configs for an Oct 4 benchmark.
[03:23] Liam O'Connor: expectation is around 200 peak QPS across a mix of seq lengths: 60% short (<128), 30% mid (128-512), 10% long (>512).
[03:33] Samir Patel: great — i'll add that to action items.

[03:50] (00:03:50) Jorge Alvarez: quick commercial thought, what does pricing look like if we run this as a co-managed setup vs us pointing customers to Redwood hosted?
[03:58] Samir Patel: there are two levers — Dedicated reservation for steady state where you commit capacity, or usage-based for hosted fallbacks. for a co-managed pilot we usually propose a small monthly reserved pool and usage overlay for overflow. i'll follow up with a template.
[04:15] Priya Menon: on security docs — do you have SOC2 and penetration test reports we can share internally?
[04:21] Maya Chen: yes, we'll share SOC2 and our pen test summary, plus an architecture diagram for V P C peering and private control plane.
[04:28] Liam O'Connor: network topology question — we prefer a model where traffic terminates inside our V P C and tokens are validated locally; can Redwood's routing TTL and prefix cache be configured to avoid cross-site hops?
[04:41] Alex Graves: yes, policies can pin to region and to your pool; also we support prefix caching locally but you have to enable the on-prem kv cache option in the config. sometimes the docs call it 'prefix cache' or 'K V cache' inconsistently.

[05:05] (00:05:05) Samir Patel: can we talk about success criteria for the pilot? what does win look like for Veridian?
[05:11] Priya Menon: low-bar win: connector deployed, routing works, and we can hit 200 QPS in synthetic runs. mid-bar: latency within target (p50 < 120 ms for short seqs) and no tenancy leaks. stretch: we can push 2x and evaluate cost/op.
[05:25] Maya Chen: got it — we'll aim to document those and bake them into the acceptance criteria.

[06:00] (00:06:00) Liam O'Connor: practical question — where do customers authenticate? we have S S O via SAML and an identity broker — ideally we'd integrate so customers don't manage separate keys.
[06:10] Alex Graves: we support SAML/SSO and token exchange flows. for the pilot we can do a short-lived token exchange: your identity broker issues a platform token which the connector exchanges to get a per-request token for the runtime.

[06:45] (00:06:45) Jorge Alvarez: any red flags from your side? things you see with other partners that trip up pilots?
[06:50] Maya Chen: common issues: network MTU mismatch with GPU NICs, unexpected egress rules blocking health checks, and mismatch in sequence distribution skews. also sometimes legal wants to rework audit log retention. we can send a pre-flight checklist.
[07:06] Priya Menon: please do — our infra team will appreciate specifics.

[07:35] (00:07:35) Samir Patel: i'll note to send the pre-flight and the onboarding checklist.

[08:00] Alex Graves: technical note — if you run mixed model families on the same pool we recommend isolating heavy long-seq models to a separate GPU partition to avoid head-of-line blocking.
[08:12] Priya Menon: makes sense. we can carve pools by instance family.

[08:40] (00:08:40) Liam O'Connor: what about telemetry — can we ingest per-request tracing? our ops team wants per-tenant latency histograms.
[08:48] Maya Chen: yes, Redwood Console exposes token-level traces and per-route histograms. we can stream metrics (Prometheus/OTLP) into your observability stack. for the pilot we'll enable a low-cardinality set, then open it up.

[09:20] (00:09:20) Jorge Alvarez: any requirements on the kernel side for your runtime for certain GPUs? we use a mix of A100 and some custom NVLink clusters.
[09:30] Alex Graves: kernel selection matters; our compilation layer auto-selects kernels but GPU driver versions must be within supported matrix. we will share the supported driver list. for NVLink topologies we sometimes need tuning parameters.

[10:00] (00:10:00) Priya Menon: ok, i'm going to summarize the dependencies from our side: provide instance SKUs + driver versions, confirm V P C peering subnet ranges, share identity broker details for token exchange, and confirm compliance contact.
[10:12] Samir Patel: perfect — i'll put those as action items.

[11:00] (00:11:00) Maya Chen: one more operational note — if you want fallback to Redwood hosted, we can configure automatic overflow routing with a cost/latency policy, though that requires cross-account billing and an overlay SLA.
[11:14] Liam O'Connor: noted — commercially we need to vet that.

[11:40] (00:11:40) Sidetrack / small crosstalk — brief noise; auto-detect mis-heard phrase logged as 'red-wood private' in transcript.

[12:10] (00:12:10) Samir Patel: ok i'll recap: Redwood to send sandbox quickstart, perf guide, SOC2 & pen test summary, and pricing template. Veridian to share SKUs, qps distribution, V P C peering details, and compliance contact. target deep-dive Oct 4.
[12:28] Priya Menon: that works.

[12:40] (00:12:40) Jorge Alvarez: one more, any examples of other partners doing co-managed pilots we can peer with?
[12:47] Samir Patel: i'll connect you with a prior integrator (subject to permission) and share a short case study doc.

[13:10] (00:13:10) Maya Chen: i'll also include a short checklist for the infra team — MTU, driver matrix, healthcheck endpoints, and firewall rules.

[13:28] Liam O'Connor: timeline ok — we'll aim to have the SKUs and contacts by end of week.

[13:40] (00:13:40) Samir Patel: brilliant. any open questions before we wrap?
[13:45] Priya Menon: no, just to confirm the sandbox will be non-production and limited retention on logs?
[13:51] Maya Chen: yes sandbox retention default is 7 days, can be adjusted for pilot but we'd recommend keeping it short for privacy.

[14:10] (00:14:10) Liam O'Connor: okay thanks everyone.
[14:13] Samir Patel: thanks — we'll follow up with the materials and schedule.

[47:55] (00:47:55) Call ended. Notes: minor transcription errors possible; action items above.
